steers.title: Losing streak: 13/20 recent trades lost
steers.detail: Win rate 30% over last 20 trades. Total PnL: -0.89 USDT. Something is wrong.

deep_analysis:
Market: BTC 74928 pinned AT continuum EMA300 (74896) for ~259m — chop pin, no resolution. zscore STRONG_POS but volume_regime LOW, linreg LEAN_BULL while market_phase DECLINING. 15m aggregate LONG_BIAS (24L/7S/92N of 123 tokens) but regimes.BTC = NEUTRAL — the two sources disagree, quote the source. BTC 15m direction flipped 31x/24h (p95 = 26, unusually unstable); aggregate flipped 19x (normal). Auto-trader sits in CHOP, score long 5 / short -5, decision BRACKET.

Both open trades are LONG in a tape where the last 7d's profitable side was SHORT (SHORT 36T +0.18 USDT 61% WR vs LONG 87T -1.35 USDT 50.6% WR). Neither trade is thesis-broken yet (both <1% up, <1h old, no stale/BE/trail rule tripped), but neither has trend support: BTC is pinned mid-band, so these are bounce-catch entries, not trend-follow entries.

SOL LONG 16848 (+0.49%) is the better of the two — entered at meta_rsi 23.68 (deep oversold) and is working. SUPER LONG 16847 (+0.32%) is the weaker one: entered at meta_rsi 73.68, above hh-hl's own LONG ceiling (HH_HL_RSI_LONG_MAX=68), and hh-hl+ is 0 wins / -0.41 USDT across the watchdog window with 1 closed trade in 7d. Live flag (HH_HL_PLUS_ENABLED=True), but n is too small to propose a kill — the action is position-level, not family-level.

Immediate contradiction risk: signals.json carries a PENDING SOL SHORT (rsi 76.19) and PENDING BTC SHORT (rsi 86.01) from jup_yolo_mirrored. If the SOL short fills while 16848 is open, we are hedged against ourselves on the same coin. Watch for it before adding anything.

Chop-bleed KPI (dollar share, NULL-inclusive): 7d 92.8% (50 of 56 losers never armed) and 14d 95.3% (145 of 157), NULL mfe_pct losers = 0 in both windows, same-day arm rate 50% (2 of 4). BOTH windows are >=92% — the loss is coming from entries that never reached +0.40% MFE, i.e. entry quality, not exit management. Route to entry-quality filters; exit tweaks will not touch this.

Regime flip context for any direction-flavored steer: aggregate 19 flips/24h, BTC 15m 31 flips/24h (>=26 p95). An average direction state survives ~1h, so do not read a single snapshot as a trend. The genuinely informative reading is BTC AT EMA300 for 259m — a real chop pin, not churn.
regime_context:
Source split: aggregate 15m = LONG_BIAS (24 long / 7 short / 92 neutral of 123 tokens); regimes.BTC 15m = NEUTRAL; 4h regime_summary = LONG_BIAS both; continuum BTC = AT EMA300 (74896 vs price 74928), linreg LEAN_BULL, zscore STRONG_POS, volume LOW, market_phase DECLINING. Auto-trader regime = CHOP (long 5 / short -5, BRACKET).

Flip rate last 24h: aggregate 19 (normal, p50=19), BTC 15m 31 (>= p95 26 = unusually unstable). Baseline 2026-10-23 was aggregate 22 / BTC 20.

Meaning for positions: we are long-only into a BTC chop pin with unstable 15m direction. No regime kill applies (BTC 4h is LONG_BIAS, no blanket block), but there is no trend tailwind either — these two longs must stand on their own structure, which is why SUPER (overbought entry, 0-win family) is the one to protect first. Condition to re-test next cycle: if BTC 1m holds above continuum EMA300 (74896) the LONG bias is intact; if it closes below for 3+ consecutive 1m closes, the long-side premise is gone.
pattern_alerts:
VERIFIED (PostgreSQL, run this cycle):

1) NEVER-ARMED CHOP ENTRIES OWN THE BLEED — dollar share of gross loss from trades with mfe_pct<0.40: 7d 92.8% (50 of 56 losers), 14d 95.3% (145 of 157 losers). NULL mfe_pct losers = 0 in both windows (no backfill distortion). Same-day arm rate 50% (2 of 4). Both windows >=92% -> entry-quality problem, not exits. WINNING SIDE = trades that reached +0.40% and rode the trail: all 6 winners in the last 20 closes exited via profit-monster-trail or cut_loser (FARTCOIN +1.66, GRASS +1.48, WLFI +0.96, MON +1.17, BTC +0.81, AVAX +0.49). Why weren't we on it: we entered before structure confirmed, so price never reached the arm level.

2) DIRECTION SPLIT 7d — LONG 87T / 44 wins / -1.35 USDT (50.6% WR) vs SHORT 36T / 22 wins / +0.18 USDT (61.1% WR). WINNING SIDE = SHORTS. We are currently 2 long / 0 short. Not an action by itself (aggregate regime is LONG_BIAS), but it is why no third long should be added while BTC sits on the pin.

3) BIG LOSERS LAST 20 CLOSES, all LONG, all never-armed: JUP -4.21% (mfe 0.02), DOGE -4.30% (mfe -0.03, hard_max_loss), BTC -3.71% (mfe 0.07, hard_max_loss), CC -2.73% (mfe 0.35), GMX -2.70% (mfe -0.07), BTC -2.53% (mfe 0.15). WINNING SIDE = the short that took the other side of each of those dumps, or simply flat. Two of them are hard_max_loss exits = classic chop entries that never had a trend to follow.

4) jup_yolo_mirrored — steer-003 claims "3 consecutive losses, -0.31 over last 20". Measured 7d: 47 closed trades, +0.16 USDT, 31 wins (66% WR). Family is flat-POSITIVE in 7d; the recent losing run (SOL SHORT -4.17, ETH SHORT -3.59, BTC SHORT -1.78) was shorts entered mid-squeeze. ENABLED and live (47 trades/7d) -> NO kill action; the steer's window is too small to act on. The three shorts lost because they shorted into a bounce, i.e. wrong side of momentum, not because the family is dead.

5) bb-squeeze+ 7d: 20T, 12 wins (60% WR) but -0.24 USDT net — winners small, losers (CC, GMX) large and never-armed. Not a kill candidate (WR fine, enabled, live); it is pattern 1 again wearing a different signal name.

6) ai-trader-pending 7d: 6T, 1 win, -0.07 USDT. hl_copy_trader 7d: 7T, 2 wins, -0.22 USDT. Both live, both small-n — monitor only.
